zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
# 招聘疲弱支撐短債，更多聯準會官員警告通膨風險

## 勞動與服務價格分歧，債市漲勢收窄

民間招聘低於預期，帶動短天期美債上漲；但服務業價格壓力與聯準會官員的新警告，使前兩天的全面反彈暫歇。2年期殖利率下降2個基點至4.18%，5年期及10年期維持4.33%、4.63%，30年期微降1個基點至5.17%。

ADP公布民間就業增加44,000人，低於預估70,000人及上月修正後95,000人。服務業調查卻沒有同樣令人安心：S&P Global終值升至54.6，ISM整體指數則幾乎持平於54.1，但就業收縮、價格支付指數達70.3。招聘可能正在放緩，國內成本壓力卻未必同步減輕。

這項分歧也貫穿聯準會發言。堪薩斯城聯準銀行總裁Jeff Schmid認為政策限制程度不足，明尼亞波利斯總裁Neel Kashkari再次主張逐步升息；支持7月維持利率的理事Lisa Cook也表示，若通膨未很快恢復下降，她準備採取行動。可能支持緊縮的範圍，已不限於先前投下異議票的官員。

財政部維持付息券規模穩定的指引，排除了眼前一項供給疑慮，但下週$1,250億季度再融資標售仍須找到買方。10年期通膨補償下降1個基點，恰被實質殖利率上升1個基點抵銷。能源風險降低仍有幫助，卻已不足以帶動整條殖利率曲線下移。

## Cook加入警告，季度再融資規模維持不變

2年期反彈使2s10s擴大2個基點至45、2s30s擴大1個基點至99，逆轉週二的小幅趨平。指標年期殖利率近一週普遍下降3至4個基點，但近一個月仍上升：2年期4個基點、5年期10個基點、10年期14個基點、30年期19個基點。長債收復先前失地的程度仍較小。

10年期抗通膨債解釋了名目殖利率為何收平。損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點至2.22%，實質殖利率卻上升1個基點至2.41%。近一個月，實質殖利率升15個基點，損益兩平通膨率反而降1個基點。長期借款成本的上升，並沒有對應到平均通膨補償的相同漲幅。

數據讓政策辯論兩方都有依據。ADP增加44,000個民間職位，低於市場預期，大型、中型及小型企業招聘均轉弱。S&P Global服務業PMI終值卻由51.2升至54.6，高於初值53.6；就業擴張速度為8個月最快，投入成本通膨則達14個月高點。

ISM的就業訊號不同。整體指數由54.0微升至54.1，低於預估54.5；企業活動升至59.1、新訂單升至57.2，就業卻回到47.4的收縮區間，價格支付指數加速至70.3。這些調查不能互相替代：合併來看，服務需求及成本仍具韌性，招聘訊號則分歧，週五官方就業報告因此更重要。

今年沒有投票權的Schmid認為，需求與投資強勁，代表政策限制程度不夠。他不接受供給造成的通膨必然自行消退，因為持續性也取決於聯準會如何回應，以及政策鼓勵了什麼行為。較低油價可以改善當前物價，卻未必能化解這項疑慮。

Kashkari在7月投下異議票後，再次表明偏好升息25個基點。他支持現在開始逐步調整，但對9月仍未確定，並將後續行動繫於通膨是否持平或惡化。Cook的警告則擴大了討論範圍，因為她先前支持維持利率。她認為關稅影響、較低油價及AI相關壓力減輕，可能使升息不再必要；但通膨已連續5年高於目標，也增加其延續至薪資與價格的風險。

市場並未單純跟隨鷹派談話。即使異議官員、支持維持利率的理事與無投票權官員都提出警告，2年期殖利率仍下跌。它仍高於3.5%至3.75%的政策利率區間，但較弱民間招聘及能源壓力減輕，降低了短端對立即行動的需求。5年期及10年期收平，則顯示買方較不願把這份紓解延伸到更遠年期。

季度再融資公告對短期供給給了更明確答案。財政部維持名目付息券及浮動利率債規模，並保留至少未來幾季不變的預期。下週$1,250億標售預計籌得約$287億新增現金，未來若增發，仍偏好放在較短年期。

官員同時把評估未來「增加」的措辭，改成評估未來「變化」。搭配美國財政部借款諮詢委員會要求保留彈性，2027財政年度發行組合仍可能調整。本季借款需求為$7,390億；更多依賴國庫券，可限制眼前存續期間供給，卻使融資成本對政策利率保持敏感。30年期期限溢酬本週達1.56%，創2013年以來最高，即使當日殖利率變動很小。

## AI供給壓力反映在既有債券

美國信用基金幾乎持平：LQD跌0.02%，HYG跌0.04%，JNK跌0.08%。更具體的壓力來自科技債。7月Meta債券平均利差擴大約22個基點、Oracle擴大29個基點，投資人既評估AI投資回報，也須為新供給騰出空間。Amazon上月$250億發行，就曾促使經理人賣出既有科技債，以籌資買進新券。

供給壓力也正跨出美元市場。Alphabet已首次大額發行英鎊與瑞郎債，也使用歐元融資。更多歐洲供給，可能縮小先前因美國投資組合承接較多科技借款而形成的相對估值優勢。美國2026年AI投資估計接近但不到$6,000億，約GDP的1.8%；2027年占比預估2.5%，2028年2.8%。支出現在就支持經濟活動，但相應債務可能在預期收入實現前，先要求更高讓利。

私募貸款人也被要求承作大型交易，成本並不低。Ares牽頭擬議$22億直接貸款，支應MedImpact Holdings收購Medical Card System，價格至少為基準利率加8個百分點。私募信貸歷經紀錄贖回後，這種規模的融資值得關注，但擬議利差也顯示貸款人對收購風險要求的補償。

United Launch Alliance另尋求透過真正的私募債安排，籌集約$5億再融資。這家Boeing與Lockheed Martin合資公司選擇非公開管道，最終價格與需求仍未確定。

Pfleiderer債券持有人則由放款人轉向股東。持有其2029年債券逾80%的債權人，同意在整體重整中取得控制權，距離前次流動性交易僅8個月。當時公司透過Monarch Alternative Capital及股東貸款籌得EUR1.35億，以轉出既有債權人保障範圍的一家子公司作為融資基礎；該事業曾被形容為最強的現金來源。

持續現金消耗與歐洲建築需求疲弱，耗盡了這段過渡融資的效果。債券持有人如今提供約EUR8,700萬新資金，其中包含EUR4,700萬初始承諾，支撐控制權移轉期間的流動性。資產轉移可以改變債權人的回收分配，卻未必解決最初迫使公司借新錢的營運缺口。這與AI供給讓利是不同風險，平穩的信用基金價格也難以呈現。

## 印度維持利率帶動反彈，中國找到長債買方

印度央行一致決議，連續第4次會議維持附買回利率5.25%，並保留中性立場。5年期公債殖利率降8個基點，10年期降3個基點至6.78%。央行未釋出回收流動性訊號，總裁對利率又保持耐心，短端因此受惠最多。市場隱含10月升息機率，由前一天100%降至65%。

預測並未顯示需求疲弱。央行把截至2027年3月年度成長預估由6.6%升至6.7%，1至3月成長曾達7.8%；截至3月年度通膨則由5.1%降至5%。印度約90%原油仰賴進口，食品與燃料仍可能推升整體通膨，部分地區雨量不足，民生消費公司也準備再漲價。此次維持利率是基於基礎壓力溫和，而非供給風險已不存在。

泰國7月CPI年增率由2.42%降至1.95%，低於預期；物價月減0.73%，6月為月減0.34%，核心通膨卻由1.23%微升至1.34%。菲律賓通膨降至6.2%，低於6月及調查中位數的6.4%，核心通膨也6個月來首次放緩，但米價仍上漲17.1%。央行今年已升息50個基點，仍準備進一步緊縮；披索上漲0.7%，只提供部分進口成本紓解。

捷克也有整體與國內價格分歧。7月通膨1.7%，符合預期，連續第二個月低於2%目標；服務通膨卻由4.5%加速至4.7%，核心先前接近3%。央行6月升息後，預期維持3.75%，市場仍保留未來一年再升息一至兩次的可能。

中國境外主權債標售，則顯示長天期人民幣債需求強勁。財政部各發行CNY10億15年及30年債，殖利率為紀錄低點1.99%、2.24%。各年期整體投標倍數4.67，為2025年6月以來最高；此前境內10年期殖利率已降至1.71%。美國30年期仍在5%以上時，買方願意延長人民幣存續期間。

日本匯率干預獲得更明確的美國支持。財長確認已買進日圓，並表示未來操作可使用FIMA附買回機制。以美債擔保借美元，可避免立即賣券；但每個交易對手每日$600億上限，接近近期其中一次干預估計規模，價格也屬備援安排。日本另有估計$1,620億存款及持續到期的美國國庫券，在必須出售長期付息券前，仍有其他美元來源。

這些選項影響市場運作，但外資需求不全由干預決定。海外投資人5月持有$9.4兆美債，年增4%；持倉仍增加，並非全面撤退，只是未跟上美國借款成長。因此其他主權曲線需求強勁，仍會在邊際上影響美國供給的承接。

## 加彭與塞內加爾，因財政可信度拉開差距

美元指數下降0.20%之際，EMB小跌0.05%，15年期以上新興市場美元主權債指數卻漲0.30%，並未出現一致的硬通貨債漲勢。更重要的差異，在於個別主權的查核結果與官方支持前景。

加彭與塞內加爾1月利差都在美債上方約1,000個基點；如今加彭收窄至約608個基點，塞內加爾卻擴大至1,541個基點。加彭在IMF支持下的審計顯示債務較低，使市場期待不必重整就能取得IMF計畫。塞內加爾審計反而揭露$70億先前隱藏借款，恢復2024年以來暫停的貸款安排也陷入僵局。

加彭已把改善的前景轉成2033年到期、$9.2億私募融資，但殖利率達12.65%，為今年新興主權最高。之後殖利率降至約11.5%，仍高於同評等非洲發行人平均10.7%。今年迄今報酬19.5%後，投資人週三獲利了結，使其2029年及2031年美元債表現落後。完整審計仍待公布，私募紓解了短期義務，並未結束財政疑問；塞內加爾則仍部分依靠國內借款付款，外部計畫支持尚未恢復。

油價壓力減輕之際，天氣又帶來另一項挑戰。聖嬰現象增強已使秘魯關閉鯷魚漁場，該產業通常支撐最多$18億出口；截至8月3日，印度雨量比正常少12%。歷史分析顯示，典型聖嬰事件可使菲律賓與印尼通膨增加近2個百分點。食品、水力發電及出口收入損失，可能抵銷部分能源降價好處，尤其對財政或匯率緩衝較弱的經濟體。

印尼成長優於預期，刺激空間卻有限。第2季GDP年增5.29%，高於預估中位數5.14%，但低於第1季5.61%；固定投資增6.87%，政府支出近16%。政府追求6%成長，並編列下半年約$15億獎勵措施。然而，法定赤字上限為GDP的3%，財政疑慮又已促使印尼盾單季下跌5%，都限制進一步支持。

哈薩克考慮約$5億熊貓債，接續5月首次CNY34億發行。該次訂單超過發行量兩倍，並創下中國境內市場BBB級主權最低票息。後續交易仍取決於市場條件及外部赤字融資需求，目的在分散這個投資級商品出口國的資金來源，而非單純再增加美元債。

美國固定收益市場收盤後，巴西如預期降息25個基點至14%，自3月累計降100個基點。理事會一致通過，但未提供前瞻指引，後續仍視數據決定；2028年第1季通膨預測3.2%，目標為3%。7月上旬通膨已由4.8%降至4.52%，但財政刺激、強勁需求與天氣仍使風險偏向上行。這次實際降息更新了先前預期，並不承諾之後加快腳步。

## 股市暫歇，黃金持續上漲

大盤四個交易日增加約$3.7兆市值後，S&P 500下跌0.17%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.83%，半導體下跌1.40%。VIX卻降4.18%至15.81。股市小跌、波動率下降，比較像強勁反彈後暫歇，而非金融壓力突然升高。

油價在先前重挫後趨穩。WTI報跌0.73%、收$75.22，布蘭特幾乎持平於$79.45。伊朗與阿曼同意一條擬議的荷莫茲航線，但更廣的60天安排仍在討論，青年運動再度威脅也使實際通航正常化更複雜。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點，顯示眼前風險再減輕一些，卻被實質殖利率上升抵銷。

美元降至99.69，黃金大漲3.67%至$4,245.80。即使10年期美債殖利率4.63%、長端高於5%，股票波動率又下降，黃金需求仍在。政策不確定性、匯率干預與地緣政治再惡化的可能，仍與其他市場的有序交易並存。

## 先看就業，再迎季度再融資標售

週五官方就業報告，將顯示ADP疲弱的44,000人增幅，是否反映更廣泛的招聘放緩。就業擴散程度、失業率與薪資需要一起看。招聘弱但薪資壓力持續，仍無法化解Cook及Schmid的通膨疑慮；更強勞動需求則支持Kashkari逐步升息的主張。服務業調查已顯示，招聘放緩本身未必能帶來成本壓力下降。

荷莫茲接下來需要落實。簽署臨時安排、接受航線並提供安全保證，才能使航運與保險正常化。最新伊朗—阿曼協議是進展，但通行費、安全爭議及青年運動干擾，仍可能阻礙過程。持續的通航恢復，才會使油價下跌成為較持久的通膨因素。

財政部維持規模後，下週$1,250億季度再融資標售將檢驗真實需求。若須大幅讓利、非交易商參與偏弱，或標售後曲線再次轉陡，市場焦點就會從延後的2027年調整，轉向當前承接能力。有序標售則讓投資人有更多空間回應勞動與通膨數據。下一次FIMA揭露可另外觀察日本是否以擔保借款、而非賣出美債取得美元；即使有大量存款及國庫券到期，這項選擇仍值得追蹤。

overall_summary.headline: 招聘疲弱支撐短債，更多聯準會官員警告通膨風險
overall_summary.session_narrative:
ADP民間就業僅增加44,000人，低於預估70,000人，帶動2年期殖利率下降2個基點至4.18%。服務調查卻分歧：S&P Global轉強，ISM則同時出現就業收縮與價格支付指數70.3。10年期殖利率維持4.63%，通膨補償下降被實質殖利率上升抵銷。

# Weak hiring helps short Treasuries as more Fed officials warn on inflation

## The rally narrows as labor and service prices diverge

Short Treasuries gained after weaker private hiring, but the broader rally of the previous two sessions stalled as service-sector price pressure and fresh Fed warnings complicated the outlook. The two-year yield fell 2 basis points to 4.18%; five- and ten-year yields held at 4.33% and 4.63%, while the 30-year eased 1 basis point to 5.17%.

ADP reported 44,000 additional private jobs, below the 70,000 forecast and a revised 95,000 in the preceding month. The service surveys offered less reassurance. S&P Global's final index rose to 54.6, while ISM's headline was almost steady at 54.1 but paired contracting employment with a prices-paid reading of 70.3. Hiring could be slowing without a comparable easing in domestic cost pressure.

That distinction ran through Fed communication. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid judged policy insufficiently restrictive. Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari again favored gradual increases, while Governor Lisa Cook, who supported July's hold, said she was ready to act if disinflation did not resume soon. The potential support for tightening extended beyond the officials who had already dissented.

Treasury removed an immediate supply concern by retaining steady coupon-size guidance, although next week's $125 billion refunding still needs buyers. At ten years, a 1-basis-point decline in inflation compensation was offset by a 1-basis-point rise in the real yield. Lower energy risk was helping, but it no longer pulled the entire yield curve down with it.

## Cook joins the warning as refunding sizes stay steady

The two-year rally steepened 2s10s by 2 basis points to 45 and 2s30s by 1 to 99, reversing Tuesday's modest flattening. Benchmark yields were 3–4 basis points lower over a week. Over a month, however, they remained higher by 4 basis points at two years, 10 at five, 14 at ten and 19 at 30. The long bond had recovered less of the earlier selloff.

Ten-year inflation-linked pricing explained the flat nominal close. The breakeven fell 1 basis point to 2.22%, while the real yield rose 1 to 2.41%. Over a month, that real yield was up 15 basis points and the breakeven down 1. The increase in longer-term borrowing costs was therefore not matched by a similar rise in average inflation compensation.

The data left room for both sides of the policy debate. ADP's 44,000 private-job gain fell short of consensus, with hiring weakening across large, midsized and small businesses. S&P Global's final Services PMI instead rose from 51.2 to 54.6, above the 53.6 flash estimate. Its employment measure expanded at the fastest pace in eight months, and input-cost inflation reached a 14-month high.

ISM told a different employment story. The headline edged from 54.0 to 54.1, below the 54.5 forecast. Business activity rose to 59.1 and new orders to 57.2, but employment returned to contraction at 47.4. Prices paid accelerated to 70.3. These are not interchangeable surveys: together, they showed resilient service demand and costs alongside conflicting hiring signals, ahead of Friday's government jobs report.

Schmid, a nonvoter this year, argued that strong demand and investment meant policy was not restrictive enough. He rejected the idea that supply-driven inflation necessarily fades by itself; persistence also depends on the Fed's response and the behavior that response encourages. Cheaper oil could help current prices without resolving that concern.

Kashkari repeated his preference for a quarter-point increase after dissenting in July. He favored beginning gradual adjustment now, but remained unsure about September and tied further moves to inflation moving sideways or worsening. Cook's warning widened the discussion because she had voted for the hold. She saw tariff effects, lower oil and easing AI-related pressure as reasons a hike might become unnecessary, while cautioning that five years of above-target inflation increased the risk of persistence in wages and prices.

Markets did not simply follow the hawkish remarks. The two-year yield declined despite warnings from a dissenter, a hold voter and a nonvoter. It remained above the 3.5%–3.75% funds range, but softer private hiring and diminished energy pressure reduced the urgency priced at the front end. Unchanged five- and ten-year yields showed less willingness to extend that relief further out.

The refunding announcement provided a clearer near-term answer on supply. Treasury kept nominal coupon and floating-rate note sizes unchanged and retained the expectation of steady sizes for at least the next several quarters. Next week's $125 billion of refunding auctions is expected to raise about $28.7 billion in new cash. Any future increases would still be directed preferentially toward shorter maturities.

Officials also changed the wording from evaluating future “increases” to evaluating future “changes.” Together with the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee's call for flexibility, that leaves room to alter the issuance mix in fiscal 2027. Current-quarter borrowing needs are $739 billion; greater reliance on bills limits near-term duration supply but keeps financing costs sensitive to the policy rate. The 30-year term premium reached 1.56% this week, its highest since 2013, even as the day's yield moves remained small.

## AI supply weighs on outstanding bonds

US credit funds barely moved: LQD fell 0.02%, HYG 0.04% and JNK 0.08%. More specific evidence of pressure came from technology bonds. Meta spreads widened about 22 basis points on average during July and Oracle spreads widened 29, as investors weighed AI returns and made room for new debt. Amazon's $25 billion sale last month had prompted portfolio managers to sell outstanding technology bonds to fund purchases of the new issue.

That supply pressure is extending beyond dollars. Alphabet has made large debut sales in sterling and Swiss francs and has also tapped euros. More European issuance could narrow the relative valuation advantage that developed while US portfolios absorbed a disproportionate share of technology borrowing. Estimated US AI investment is just under $600 billion in 2026, or 1.8% of GDP, with the share projected to reach 2.5% in 2027 and 2.8% in 2028. The spending supports activity now, while the accompanying debt can demand concessions before the expected revenue arrives.

Private lenders were also being asked to finance large transactions, at substantial cost. Ares was leading a proposed $2.2 billion direct loan for MedImpact Holdings' acquisition of Medical Card System, priced at least 8 percentage points over the benchmark. A financing of that size would be notable after record redemptions unsettled private credit, but its proposed spread underscores the compensation being sought for acquisition risk.

United Launch Alliance was separately seeking about $500 million through a true private placement to refinance debt. The Boeing–Lockheed Martin joint venture was pursuing a nonpublic route; neither final pricing nor demand had yet established the transaction's terms.

Pfleiderer's bondholders were moving from lending to ownership. Holders of more than 80% of the company's 2029 notes agreed to take control in a broader restructuring, only eight months after an earlier liquidity transaction. That financing had raised EUR135 million from Monarch Alternative Capital and a shareholder loan against a unit moved beyond existing creditors' reach. The transferred business had been described as the strongest cash generator.

Continued cash burn and weak European construction demand exhausted the benefit of that bridge. Bondholders have now provided about EUR87 million of new financing, including EUR47 million of initial commitments, to support liquidity during the transfer. The sequence shows how an asset transfer can change creditor recoveries without resolving the operating shortfall that made new financing necessary. It is a different risk from AI supply concessions, and one that a quiet day for broad credit funds does little to reveal.

## India rallies on a hold; China finds long-duration buyers

The Reserve Bank of India unanimously kept its repo rate at 5.25% for a fourth meeting and retained a neutral stance. Five-year government yields fell 8 basis points and ten-year yields fell 3 to 6.78%. The absence of a liquidity-absorption signal, alongside the governor's patience on rates, helped the front end most. The market-implied probability of an October increase fell from 100% the previous day to 65%.

The forecasts did not describe weak demand. The RBI raised growth for the year ending March 2027 from 6.6% to 6.7%, after 7.8% growth in January–March, while lowering inflation for the year through March from 5.1% to 5%. India imports roughly 90% of its crude. Food and fuel could still lift headline inflation, rainfall was deficient in parts of the country, and consumer companies were preparing more price increases. The hold rested on muted underlying pressure rather than an absence of supply risks.

Thailand's July CPI slowed from 2.42% to 1.95%, below expectations. Prices fell 0.73% on the month after June's 0.34% decline, although core inflation edged from 1.23% to 1.34%. Philippine inflation eased to 6.2%, below both June and the 6.4% survey median, and core slowed for the first time in six months. Rice prices were still up 17.1%. After raising rates 50 basis points this year, the central bank remained prepared to tighten; the peso's 0.7% gain provided only some relief from import costs.

The Czech Republic showed a similar split between headline and domestic prices. July inflation was 1.7%, in line with expectations and below the 2% target for a second month, but services accelerated from 4.5% to 4.7% and core had been near 3%. The central bank was expected to hold at 3.75% after its June increase. Markets still allowed one to two more hikes over a year.

China's offshore sovereign auction demonstrated strong demand for long yuan bonds. The finance ministry sold CNY1 billion each of 15- and 30-year debt at record-low yields of 1.99% and 2.24%. Across maturities, bid-to-cover was 4.67, the highest since June 2025. The result followed a fall in the onshore ten-year yield to 1.71%. Buyers were willing to extend in yuan even while the US 30-year yield remained above 5%.

Japan's currency intervention received more explicit US backing. Its finance minister confirmed yen purchases and said authorities could use FIMA repo for future operations. Borrowing dollars against Treasuries can avoid immediate outright sales, although the $60 billion daily counterparty cap is close to the estimated size of one recent intervention and pricing is designed for a backstop. Japan also has an estimated $162 billion in deposits and recurring Treasury-bill maturities, providing other dollars before long coupons need to be sold.

Those funding options matter for market functioning, but not all foreign demand is intervention-related. Overseas investors held $9.4 trillion of Treasuries in May, 4% more than a year earlier. Their holdings were growing, not retreating wholesale, but had not kept pace with US borrowing growth. Stronger demand for other sovereign curves can therefore still matter at the margin for US supply.

## Gabon and Senegal separate on fiscal credibility

EMB slipped 0.05% while the 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign index gained 0.30%, despite a 0.20% decline in the Dollar Index. There was no uniform hard-currency rally. More consequential differences appeared in individual sovereigns whose financing prospects depended on audits and official support.

Gabon and Senegal both traded near 1,000 basis points over Treasuries in January. Gabon's spread has since narrowed to about 608 basis points, while Senegal's widened to 1,541. Gabon's IMF-supported audit indicated lower debt and encouraged expectations of an IMF program without restructuring. Senegal's audit uncovered $7 billion of previously hidden borrowing, and negotiations to revive a facility suspended since 2024 have stalled.

Gabon had turned its improved outlook into $920 million of private-placement funding due in 2033, but at 12.65%, the highest EM sovereign yield this year. That yield subsequently fell to about 11.5%, still above the 10.7% average for similarly rated African issuers. Its 2029 and 2031 dollar bonds lagged on Wednesday as investors took profit following a 19.5% year-to-date return. The full audit remains pending. The placement addresses short-term obligations without closing the fiscal question, while Senegal continues to make payments partly through domestic borrowing as external program support remains unresolved.

Weather poses another challenge just as oil pressure eases. A strengthening El Nino has closed Peru's anchovy fishery, which normally supports exports worth as much as $1.8 billion. Indian rainfall through August 3 was 12% below normal. Historical analysis suggests a typical episode can add nearly 2 percentage points to inflation in the Philippines and Indonesia. Food prices, hydropower and lost export receipts could thus offset some of the benefit from cheaper energy, particularly where fiscal buffers or currencies are weak.

Indonesia's growth improved relative to expectations, but stimulus had limits. Second-quarter GDP rose 5.29% from a year earlier, above the 5.14% median forecast and below the first quarter's 5.61%. Fixed investment grew 6.87% and government spending almost 16%. The government earmarked about $1.5 billion of second-half incentives while seeking 6% growth. Its statutory deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP, and scrutiny that had contributed to a 5% quarterly rupiah decline, constrained further support.

Kazakhstan was considering about $500 million of panda bonds after its CNY3.4 billion May debut attracted more than twice the amount offered and achieved the lowest coupon for a BBB-rated sovereign in China's onshore market. A follow-on would depend on market conditions and external deficit-financing needs. The prospective deal would diversify an investment-grade commodity exporter's funding rather than simply add another dollar issue.

After the US fixed-income close, Brazil delivered the expected 25-basis-point cut to 14%, bringing cumulative easing since March to 100 basis points. The unanimous board withheld forward guidance and kept further moves dependent on data. It projected inflation of 3.2% in the first quarter of 2028, against a 3% target. Annual inflation had slowed from 4.8% to 4.52% in early July, but fiscal stimulus, strong demand and weather risk continued to tilt the risks upward. The completed cut updates the earlier expectation without promising a faster subsequent cycle.

## Stocks pause while gold keeps rising

The S&P 500 fell 0.17%, the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.83% and semiconductors lost 1.40% after the broader market had added about $3.7 trillion over four sessions. VIX nevertheless fell 4.18% to 15.81. Modest equity losses alongside lower volatility looked more like a pause after a strong advance than an abrupt turn toward financial stress.

Oil stabilized after the preceding collapse. WTI was reported down 0.73% at $75.22 and Brent nearly unchanged at $79.45. Iran and Oman agreed on a proposed Hormuz shipping route, but a broader 60-day arrangement remained under discussion and renewed Houthi threats complicated physical normalization. The ten-year breakeven's 1-basis-point decline suggested some further reduction in immediate inflation risk, offset in nominal yields by the real-yield increase.

The dollar fell to 99.69 and gold jumped 3.67% to $4,245.80. Gold demand persisted even with ten-year yields at 4.63%, long yields above 5% and lower equity volatility. Policy uncertainty, currency intervention and the possibility of renewed geopolitical disruption remained relevant alongside otherwise orderly markets.

## Jobs first, then the refunding auctions

Friday's government employment report will show whether ADP's weak 44,000 gain reflects a broader hiring slowdown. Employment breadth, unemployment and wages need to be read together. Weak hiring with persistent wage pressure would leave Cook's and Schmid's inflation concerns intact; firmer labor demand would support Kashkari's preference for gradual increases. The service surveys have already shown why slower hiring alone need not deliver lower cost pressure.

Hormuz now needs implementation. A signed interim arrangement, an accepted route and security guarantees would allow shipping and insurance activity to normalize. The latest Iran-Oman agreement is progress, but tolls, security disputes and Houthi disruption can still interfere. Sustained traffic recovery would make the oil decline a more durable influence on inflation than another diplomatic headline.

Next week's $125 billion of refunding auctions will test actual demand after Treasury retained steady sizes. Large concessions, weak nondealer participation or renewed steepening afterward would shift attention from deferred 2027 changes to current absorption. Orderly sales would give the market more room to respond to labor and inflation data. The next FIMA disclosure offers a related, narrower check on whether Japan is obtaining dollars against collateral rather than selling Treasuries; its funding choices remain relevant even with substantial deposits and bill maturities available.
